results.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Flip and Motorola RAZR phones already have problems
results.content:
Two new phones with folding displays, the $1,380 Samsung Galaxy Z Flip and the $1,500 Motorola RAZR, launched in recent weeks, and people already have complaints about them.

It seems like a repeat of what we went through nearly a year ago, when Samsung seeded the Galaxy Fold to reviewers and early units broke. The phone was delayed for five months while Samsung worked on a solution, but the launch seems to have been fine after the company made changes to the hinge and screen.

But the latest foldable phones are having issues of their own. Here's what's going on.

Over the weekend, YouTube channel JerryRigEverything called into question Samsung's claims that the new Galaxy Z Flip has a glass display. [...] The Z Flip comes with a warning similar to that of the Galaxy Fold, with both a sticker on the screen and a start-up warning that tells users to "avoid pressing hard on the screen or the front camera lens" and to make sure there's nothing on the screen when you fold it closed. Samsung offers a one-time screen replacement for $119 if owners have a problem.

Samsung also told CNBC that it will offer a free screen protector for Z Flip owners at Samsung retail locations or by mail. Samsung didn't explain why that additional screen protector isn't included with the phone out of the box, though.

Meanwhile, the Motorola RAZR, which also has a foldable display, is also breaking. [...] The issues with the Motorola RAZR are a bit more serious. The screen shouldn't separate from the phone. It's not known how widespread this problem is but, even before Input reported its problems, most reviewers didn't like the phone anyway.

Until folding phones have durable glass displays that don't damage easily, or show us why they're better than cheaper phones that don't fold, you shouldn't buy one.

results.content:
What makes this especially frustrating is that I am required to use additional tokens to make edits and corrections to assets and videos that are already affected by what appear to be software-related problems. In other words, I am essentially being charged additional money to correct problems that I did not create.  
  
The customer support experience has also been extremely disappointing. I attempted to explain the issues to a representative named “Dan” so that I could get assistance resolving the problem. Before we were able to fully discuss the issue or determine whether there was a way to fix it, he immediately asked whether I wanted to cancel. When I asked whether cancellation would result in a refund, I was told that I would not be eligible for one. [...] Considering 80 reviews, most reviewers were unhappy with their experience overall. People frequently expressed strong frustration over unexpected costs, explaining that initial plans provide far too few tokens to finish generating even a single video. Consumers also pointed out that technical issues, such as distorted visuals and poor synchronization, combined with difficult cancellation processes to create a frustrating experience. However, some customers also noted that specific staff members provided prompt assistance and processed refunds quickly when mistakes happened.
